intro.title: What does Exyconn build for cafés and coffee shops?
intro.definition: is a set of agents that take orders from WhatsApp and Instagram, look after regulars, answer reviews, reorder stock and keep the rota straight, all working from the POS the café already uses. Exyconn designs, builds and runs them for single cafés and small chains. Your baristas keep making coffee; the agent handles the messages and the admin around it.

benefits.title: Why cafés are doing this now

items.text: Office crowds want to order on the walk over and collect without queueing.
Instagram DMs asking "are you open?" or "do you have vegan cake?" go unread during the morning rush.
An order placed directly with the café carries no aggregator commission.
Regulars pay the rent, and they notice when you remember their usual.
Owners still finish the rota and the supplier orders after closing, by hand.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a café's hours actually go
props.lede: Ask any café owner what eats the day besides coffee and you hear the same things.

items.title: Messages nobody can answer at 9am
items.text: Pre-order requests, table questions and catering enquiries arrive on WhatsApp and Instagram exactly when every hand is on the counter. By the time someone replies, the customer has gone elsewhere.

items.title: Loyalty on stamp cards
items.text: Stamp cards get lost, and the POS knows what people buy but nobody uses it. A regular who stops coming in just disappears without anyone noticing.

items.title: Reviews spread across apps
items.text: Google, Zomato, Swiggy and Instagram comments all need watching. A complaint about cold food on a delivery order can sit unanswered for a week.

items.title: Running out of the basics
items.text: Milk, beans, cups and lids are ordered from memory or a notebook. One missed dairy order means a morning of apologising for no oat milk.

items.title: The rota lives in a group chat
items.text: Part-time staff swap shifts by messaging each other, and the manager finds out when someone fails to turn up for the opening shift.

items.title: Menu decisions on gut feel
items.text: Which bakes sell out by noon and which get thrown away at closing is in the POS, but pulling it out takes an evening the owner doesn't have.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off the counter

items.title: Pre-orders from WhatsApp and Instagram
items.text: Takes the order in the chat, checks what's available on the POS menu, collects payment by UPI or card link and pushes the ticket to the counter with a pickup time.

items.title: Regulars who feel remembered
items.text: Keeps a digital stamp card against the customer's phone number, recalls their usual from POS history and sends a note when someone who came daily hasn't been in for two weeks.

items.title: Replies on Google and Zomato
items.text: Drafts a reply to every new review for the owner to approve and groups the complaints, so "slow at lunch" or "cold sandwiches on delivery" shows up as a pattern, not a one-off.

items.title: Stock and supplier reorders
items.text: Works out what's running low from sales and recipe usage in the POS, drafts the order for the dairy, bakery and bean suppliers, and sends it on WhatsApp once the manager says yes.

items.title: Rota and shift swaps
items.text: Publishes the weekly rota to staff on WhatsApp, handles swap requests between people who can cover, and tells the manager about any gap before the shift starts.

items.title: Daily sales and menu performance
items.text: Sends the owner a closing summary from the POS: takings by channel, best and worst sellers, what was wasted, and a plain answer to questions like "is the cold brew worth keeping?"

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a two-outlet coffee shop
props.lede: A weekday at a neighbourhood café with a second counter in an office park. Each moment lights the part of the shop the agent is working on.

moments.title: A gap in the opening shift
moments.text: A barista messages that she's unwell. The agent offers the shift to two part-timers who are free, one accepts, and the manager gets the updated rota before the shutters go up.

moments.title: The office rush, pre-ordered
moments.text: Fourteen WhatsApp pre-orders come in from the office park in half an hour. Each is paid by UPI and printed at the counter with a pickup time.

moments.title: Oat milk before it runs out
moments.text: Sales are ahead of the usual pace. The agent drafts tomorrow's dairy order with extra oat milk and sends it to the supplier after the manager taps approve.

moments.title: A regular comes back
moments.text: A customer who used to come in every morning hasn't visited in three weeks. A short message with a free cookie on his next coffee goes out; he redeems it the same afternoon.

moments.title: A Zomato complaint answered
moments.text: A delivery review says the sandwich arrived soggy. The agent drafts an apology for the owner and notes it's the second mention of packaging this week.

moments.title: Closing numbers on WhatsApp
moments.text: Takings by outlet and channel, the three bakes that sold out and the two that were binned arrive on the owner's phone before she's home.

items.question: Will this replace my counter staff?
items.answer: No. It takes the messages, stamp cards, supplier orders and rota juggling off their hands. Making coffee, talking to customers and handling a complaint in person stay with your team.

items.question: Does it work with my POS and the delivery apps?
items.answer: It works with POS systems that offer an API or a regular data export, which covers most cloud café POS tools. Orders from Swiggy and Zomato usually reach your POS through its own integration, so the agent reads them from there. In the first week we check exactly what your setup allows.

items.question: What happens if someone orders something you've run out of?
items.answer: The agent reads item availability from the POS, so a sold-out item isn't offered. If stock runs out after the order is placed, it tells the customer straight away and offers a swap or a refund.

items.question: Can customers order in Hindi or other languages?
items.answer: Yes. The agent replies in the language the customer writes in, including Hindi, Hinglish and other Indian languages, while your menu stays written once.

items.question: What about customer data and marketing messages?
items.answer: Phone numbers and order history stay in your systems and a private environment we set up for you. Offers go only to people who have opted in on WhatsApp, and customers can stop them at any time, in line with India's DPDP Act and WhatsApp's own business messaging rules.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of outlets and which jobs you switch on. Most cafés start with WhatsApp pre-orders and the stamp card; tell us about your café and we'll send a fixed quote for that first phase.
